ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. Incidental calcified granuloma, benign.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

mri.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass, haemorrhage, midline shift, or restricted diffusion. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure 148 mmH2O (normal). Nucleated cells 4/mm3. Protein 96 mg/dL (elevated). Glucose 58 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.64). Gram stain: no organisms. Culture: no growth. Elevated protein with a normal cell count (albuminocytological dissociation). Clinical correlation recommended.
Myositis-specific antibodies not detected, including anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP.

Myositis_Antibodies.clinical_significance: Anti-HMGCR antibodies are found in statin-associated immune-mediated necrotising myopathy; a negative result makes it unlikely. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Bedside respiratory function 6 h after admission: FVC 1.7 L (58% predicted; 24 mL/kg at 70 kg) L. MIP -26 cmH2O L. MEP 44 cmH2O L. Change: FVC 1.8 L to 1.7 L over 6 h (6% fall). Cough effective.

quantitative_data.previous: FVC 1.8 L, MIP -28 cmH2O 6 h earlier

output.impression: 24-hour continuous telemetry. Sinus rhythm 64-108 bpm with intermittent sinus tachycardia. No pauses and no arrhythmia. Blood pressure 132/80 to 162/94 mmHg.
output.rhythm_summary: Sinus rhythm with intermittent sinus tachycardia to 108 bpm.

interactions: IVIg and spironolactone: no pharmacokinetic interaction; both affect volume status and renal function, so creatinine, sodium and potassium are monitored during the infusion (relative caution).
IVIg and ursodeoxycholic acid: no interaction identified.
output.proposed: IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days; current medicines atorvastatin, metformin, ursodeoxycholic acid and spironolactone
warnings: Atorvastatin: statins cause myopathy, including immune-mediated necrotising myopathy; the atorvastatin SmPC lists active liver disease as a contraindication and advises stopping the drug if CK rises markedly or muscle symptoms are unexplained.
Metformin: the SmPC lists hepatic insufficiency as a contraindication because of the risk of lactic acidosis.
IVIg: renal impairment and thrombosis are recognised risks; renal function is checked before infusion and hydration maintained (IVIg SmPC).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG separate a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy from a myopathy, the main competing explanation for proximal weakness on a statin [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative. Here: INR 1.9 and platelets 88 to review before the lumbar puncture, cholestatic liver tests with albumin 3.1, and CK only mildly raised (410 U/L)
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK, with coagulation before the lumbar puncture
action_criteria.rationale: Platelets and INR must be known before the lumbar puncture in decompensated liver disease; the CK level weighs the myopathy alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis; the lumbar puncture follows the platelet count and INR, with correction if the values require it [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.label: Myositis antibody panel (including anti-HMGCR) to exclude statin-associated or inflammatory myopathy
action_criteria.rationale: Proximal weakness with a raised CK on atorvastatin raises statin-associated immune-mediated necrotising myopathy and inflammatory myopathy; a negative panel with the neurogenic EMG removes them.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: She cannot stand and is still progressing; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide ICU-level care and intubation planning [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus rhythm 64-108 bpm without pauses or arrhythmia and blood pressure 132/80 to 162/94 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias, pauses and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sinus rhythm 98 bpm with normal intervals (QTc 452 ms) and no conduction or ST-T abnormality: a baseline while autonomic involvement can still develop
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and conduction abnormality and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Statin with a raised CK in decompensated liver disease, metformin in hepatic insufficiency, and spironolactone with IVIg (renal function and potassium)
action_criteria.label: Check the medication list for interactions with atorvastatin, metformin, ursodeoxycholic acid and spironolactone before IVIg
action_criteria.rationale: Her medicines include a statin while CK is raised, metformin in hepatic insufficiency and a potassium-sparing diuretic alongside IVIg: concrete interactions that change management (ROUND_POLICY ruling 6).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on immunotherapy choice in GBS with liver disease and coagulopathy
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
Do not start plasma exchange with albumin replacement without addressing INR 1.9 and platelets 88 (relative caution: it depletes clotting factors).
required_recommendations: Admit to ICU-level monitoring now: FVC 1.7 L (58% predicted, 24 mL/kg) and falling, MIP -26 cmH2O; repeat FVC, MIP and MEP every 4-6 hours and plan elective intubation if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (1.4 L at 70 kg), MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, or bulbar function, cough or secretions worsen; intubate at once for respiratory distress, hypoxaemia or hypercapnia [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, 28 g/day at 70 kg): she cannot stand (GBS disability score 4) and is still progressing at 3 weeks; plasma exchange with albumin replacement is less suitable with INR 1.9 and platelets 88 [EAN_PNS_2023].
Hold atorvastatin while CK is raised and a statin-associated myopathy is being excluded; review metformin (hepatic insufficiency, acute illness) and cover glucose with insulin as needed.
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses.
Co-manage with hepatology; monitor creatinine, sodium and potassium during IVIg (spironolactone, cirrhosis).
Mechanical DVT prophylaxis (intermittent pneumatic compression); add pharmacological prophylaxis only after weighing platelets 88 and INR 1.9.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome (acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy) after bronchitis, with primary biliary cholangitis

differential.key_features: Proximal weakness on atorvastatin with CK 410 fits, but areflexia, CSF protein 96 with 4 cells, demyelinating NCS, a neurogenic needle EMG without myopathic units and a negative myositis panel (anti-HMGCR, anti-SRP) exclude it.
Progression over 3 weeks fits GBS; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
PBC can be associated with cryoglobulinaemia and vasculitic neuropathy, typically asymmetric mononeuropathy multiplex rather than symmetric areflexic weakness with a demyelinating NCS.
Grade 1 encephalopathy with ammonia 68 explains the mild confusion but not areflexic weakness, CSF dissociation or the demyelinating NCS.
UDCA is not a recognised cause of acute polyradiculoneuropathy.

key_clinical_evidence: Progression over 3 weeks meets the GBS requirement of a nadir within 4 weeks; continued progression beyond 8 weeks would make it acute-onset CIDP [EAN_PNS_2023].

A mildly raised CK occurs in GBS; areflexia, CSF albuminocytological dissociation, a demyelinating NCS with a neurogenic needle EMG and a negative myositis panel set it apart from a statin-associated myopathy.
Vasculitic neuropathy associated with autoimmune comorbidities is typically asymmetric, distinguishing it from symmetric GBS.
FVC 58% predicted with MIP -26 cmH2O meets ICU-level monitoring triggers even though she has no bulbar weakness [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].
With INR 1.9 and platelets 88, plasma exchange with albumin replacement worsens coagulopathy; IVIg is the practical choice, with renal function monitored.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: PBC-associated neuropathy is typically asymmetric and chronic; the symmetric, ascending, areflexic profile with albuminocytological dissociation and a demyelinating NCS is GBS.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on a vasculitic or autoimmune neuropathy specific to PBC.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A mild CK rise is seen in GBS. Areflexia, the CSF dissociation, the demyelinating NCS with a neurogenic needle EMG and a negative myositis panel including anti-HMGCR exclude a statin-associated myopathy; the statin is held while this is settled.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on statin-associated or inflammatory myopathy as the cause of proximal weakness.

sequence_constraints.reason: Platelets 88 and INR 1.9 in decompensated liver disease: platelet count and coagulation must be known before the lumbar puncture, and corrected if required.
Renal function, potassium and CK are needed to read the interaction check before IVIg.

ecg.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 98. Normal intervals (QTc 452 ms). No acute ST-T wave changes.

labs.interpretation: WBC 11.4 (elevated), hemoglobin 10.8 (low), platelets 88 (low). INR 1.9 and PT 21.4 s (prolonged). Total bilirubin 3.2, ALP 428, ALT 62 and AST 74 (elevated); albumin 3.1 (low). Glucose 168 (elevated). CK 410 U/L (elevated). Ammonia 68 µmol/L (elevated). AMA positive. Remaining values within reference ranges.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

findings.finding: DML 7.6 ms (prolonged); CV 30 m/s (reduced); CMAP 2.2 mV (reduced)
DML 6.8 ms; CV 32 m/s (reduced); CMAP 2.8 mV
Absent bilateral peroneal; prolonged median 56 ms

Iliopsoas, vastus lateralis and tibialis anterior bilaterally: reduced recruitment of normal-duration, normal-amplitude motor units; occasional fibrillation potentials in tibialis anterior. Deltoid: mildly reduced recruitment. No short-duration, low-amplitude polyphasic units.

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in bilateral peroneal and tibial motor nerves, with reduced CMAP amplitudes; borderline changes in median motor nerves. 2. Absent sural sensory nerve action potentials bilaterally. 3. Absent F-waves bilaterally (peroneal); prolonged F-wave latency in bilateral median nerves (56 ms). 4. Absent H-reflex bilaterally. 5. Needle EMG: reduced recruitment of normal motor units in proximal and distal muscles with occasional fibrillation potentials distally; no myopathic units. Pattern consistent with a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with proximal involvement.

quantitative_data.pattern: Demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy, lower limb predominant, proximal involvement

metadata.difficulty_description: Raised CK on a statin with a PBC background: competing diagnoses for proximal weakness; the NCS and needle EMG are decisive
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required actions (NCS/EMG, labs with coagulation before LP, CSF, respiratory function, telemetry, interaction check), 1 recommended mimic exclusion (myositis panel), 2 red herrings (PBC, raised CK on a statin).
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Three-week progressive weakness, predominantly proximal and in the lower extremities, after bronchitis, with absent knee and ankle reflexes.

family_history: No relevant family history of neuromuscular disease
past_medical_history: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), end-stage liver disease, Child-Pugh B

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. V. is a 54-year-old woman with end-stage liver disease secondary to primary biliary cholangitis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia presenting with a 3-week history of progressive weakness. She had an episode of bronchitis approximately 4 weeks ago treated with a short course of antibiotics. About a week later she began having difficulty rising from a chair and climbing stairs; the weakness has worsened steadily, and for the last 2 days she has been unable to stand. The weakness has been primarily proximal and lower extremity-predominant. She denies any sensory symptoms, pain, or difficulty with sphincters. She has no diplopia or dysphagia. She denies alcohol use. Her atorvastatin was continued throughout. Her husband noted she seemed more confused than her baseline mild hepatic encephalopathy.

neurological_exam.coordination: Intact finger-nose bilaterally. Limited heel-shin assessment.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. No facial weakness. No ophthalmoplegia. Gag preserved.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented. Mildly encephalopathic at baseline (known hepatic encephalopathy grade 1).
neurological_exam.motor: Proximal lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 3/5 bilaterally, knee extension 3+/5. Upper extremity proximal strength 4/5. Distal strength 4+/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent bilateral patellar and Achilles. Trace bilateral biceps. Downgoing plantars.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact light touch and pinprick throughout.
